items.title: Are we talkin’ to him? Yes, it’s ROBERT DE NIRO & BEN STILLER on Focker In-Law
items.author: Kermode and Mayo's Take
items.content:
<article>Become a Vanguardista or an Ultra Vanguardista through our Patreon for full access to the Take community and the chance to shape the show. Connect with other wittertainees in our chatrooms, vote in polls to have your say in podcast features, and get exclusive behind the scenes access. Plus you’ll get Take 2 in video every week, and an extra fortnightly LIVE show with Take Ultra. Sign up here: https://www.patreon.com/c/kermodeandmayo/membership  
 
For the first time ever in Wittertainment history, we have the one and only Robert De Niro on the show. Yes that’s right, we’re talkin’ to him…. That’s alongside Ben Stiller who co-stars with him in Focker In-Law, the latest instalment in the Meet The Parents/Fockers franchise. Simon chats to them about meeting a mellower Jack in his 80s, and a Gaylord Focker shaping up to be a father-in-law to rival him. Plus, Simon squeezes in some vintage De Niro chat about the movie legend’s earliest comedy roles in the 60s, including one film that took almost a decade to release. 
 
Mark will review Focker In-Law, as well as two of the week’s biggest movies from two very different areas of the cinematic spectrum. There’s Minotaur, an excruciatingly emotional political drama set amidst Russian corruption. As Simon says, watching it comes with the added bonus of annoying Putin. Next up there’s a film that will probably annoy Mark: The Further Misadventures of Cliff Booth. It’s the latest Tarantino-penned, Fincher-directed extension to the Once Upon A Time In Hollywood universe, starring Brad Pitt. But, to use QT’s own terminology, is it ‘weak sauce’?  
 
All that, plus our new innuendous feature Ooh Matreon!, the Good Doctors’ rundown of the Box Office Top 10, and The Laughter Lift - this week featuring a lesson in Cockney rhyming slang for Mark and Simon…

items.title: FRANCIS LAWRENCE - Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 221 Francis Lawrence - Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with director Francis Lawrence (THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING, THE LONG WALK, I AM LEGEND). Many of Francis' films are based on novels or other literary properties, and throughout the episode we discuss how he approaches adapting others' work and what has changed in his own process for bringing those stories to the screen. During our discussion about his work in THE HUNGER GAMES franchise, Francis shares what it was about the novels' story that originally attracted him to direct the first sequel, and he speaks about how he prepares the films' elaborate action sequences while focusing on character. We also learn how the business of music videos gave Francis the opportunity to experiment and accumulate experience after graduating from film school, and he reveals how he made the jump into feature filmmaking. We also discuss Francis' work on I AM LEGEND, and he reflects on the unusual level of access the film had while shooting in New York City and the decision to pivot from the original ending after a series of test screenings.

This episode is sponsored by BenQ

items.title: What’s the Most Insane Thing an Actor Has Ever Done?
items.author: FilmStack
items.content:
<article>Losing over 60 pounds, learning to box for a year and a half, or hanging off the side of a plane as it takes off. Actors have gone to some ridiculous lengths to make a role feel real.

They’ve transformed their bodies, learned entirely new skills, stayed in character for months, and sometimes put themselves through productions that were almost as demanding as the characters they were playing.

So today, we’re looking at 11 of the most extreme things actors have ever done for a film. But as always, we want to hear from you. Which one do you think went the furthest?

items.title: RICHARD STYLES - Assistant Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 220 Richard Styles - Assistant Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with assistant director Richard Styles (28 YEARS LATER, THE CROWN, GOSFORD PARK). Throughout the episode, Richard helps us understand who is responsible for what, within the assistant directing team, from third to first and all the grades in between. Richard also reflects on getting his shot as a third AD on the endless production of ALIEN 3, and we discuss what he learned working as a runner and office PA in England up until then. We later discuss the puzzle of scheduling, and Richard shares his strategies and experiences for not just locking a schedule but also adjusting it as production unfolds. Richard also reflects on how he helps maintain morale on set, and he shares how he adapts to each new director he works with. Richard also shares how he, director Fernando Meirelles (Season 2, Episode 198), and cinematographer César Charlone (Season 2, Episode 174) shot the global story of THE CONSTANT GARDENER around the world, and Richard gives his advice to anyone interested in working in the film industry.

This episode is sponsored by BenQ

items.title: TIM SQUYRES - Editor
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 219 Tim Squyres - Editor

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with editor Tim Squyres (GEMINI MAN; LIFE OF PI; CROUCHING TIGER, HIDDEN DRAGON). Throughout the episode, Tim shares his thoughts on many aspects of editing, with topics ranging from finding the right cut of a scene with the director to dealing with studio notes and screening reactions. Tim also shares how he first met director Ang Lee and why he thinks they've continued to work together since 1991, and we learn how Tim cut films such as CROUCHING TIGER, HIDDEN DRAGON and LUST, CAUTION despite not understanding the film's spoken language. We also learn how Tim adapts his process to different directors, and we discuss how he feels when he receives a mountain of coverage on a scene. Tim, through his work with Ang, has cut a number of films on the edge of technological advancements from 3D projection to elevated framerates, and he shares how the process of cutting those films differs and mirrors the process of cutting a film following a traditional American cinematic format. We also discuss Tim's role as another judge for performance, and Tim shares his involvement in the sound mixing of a movie. Tim edited UNBROKEN (which we shot) and we had a wonderful time catching up with him.

This episode is sponsored by BenQ
